newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha stable despite stronger crudes.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha stable despite stronger crudes.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were mostly unchanged in slow afternoon trade on Monday despite Friday's overseas crude gains, as near-term physical cargoes remained ample in the region, traders said.
"Buyers were rather nervous to buy in such a bearish market," one trader said.
Offers for first-half July open-spec naphtha were heard at $205.00 per tonne, while bids were notionally assessed at $203.50. It was indicated at $203.00/204.50 on Friday.
Second-half June was quoted about $1.50 lower than the first-half July contract.
Contango in one-month spreads was little changed with the first-half June contract assessed $2.50 below first-half July.
Gas oil trading was unseasonably dull as domestic stockpiles remained high, traders said.
Japanese gas oil imports traditionally pick up this time of year, when many refineries are closed for routine maintenance and more drivers are on the road, they said.

Levels for jet kerosene cargoes were assessed at 80 cents to $1.10 per barrel over the mean of Singapore quotes. However, traders said the assessment was purely notional with trading dead quiet. -- Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
